analysis: The only change in this PR is one added documentation bullet in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1025, in the `darkbloom status` output list). It says App Attest serving authorization can remain visible through its unexpired lease, while MDM removal advice requires a matching fresh coordinator decision. It also says the same distinction applies to both doctor summaries, and links to ../reference/provider-authorization.md. I examined both base units, which cover the surrounding CLI reference, and found no code, config, protocol, key handling, or default changes. The wording is consistent with the retained threat model. The lease-bound authorization language matches A-016 and T-053. Gating MDM removal advice on a fresh decision matches T-057, which covers premature MDM removal stranding a provider. The text does not claim new trust, and it does not weaken the rule that a cached verdict or lease is not a substitute for current evidence. No threat-model assets, trust boundaries or mitigations change. Remaining question for integration: the referenced doc ../reference/provider-authorization.md and the doctor implementation are outside the supplied evidence. I could not verify that the code actually enforces the described fresh-decision requirement for MDM removal advice. This is a documentation-only change, so I record that as an unverified contract and not as a finding.
